executiveSummary: North Carolina Ports reported a cyberattack impacting Wilmington, Morehead City, and Charlotte Inland Port, prompting manual processing during containment and recovery. This confirms that port business systems and associated workflows remain attractive targets and that contingency procedures are essential for continuity. View Article A standing U.S. Maritime Administration advisory warns that foreign-manufactured port equipment and logistics platforms-particularly remotely serviced ship-to-shore cranes-pose elevated cyber risk through remote access, third-party connectivity, and supply-chain exposure, necessitating OT segmentation, vendor-access governance, and integrity controls. Government Advisory Available reporting indicates persistent GNSS jamming and spoofing affecting commercial shipping across multiple corridors, with both research and practitioner advisories emphasizing bridge-team vigilance and cross-checking navigation data. Supporting Report Maritime Advisory
